L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT (PDV) is a single 17% rate nationwide (no reduced rate), with exports zero-rated. Registration is required once taxable supplies exceed or are likely to exceed BAM 100,000 (doubled from BAM 50,000 in December 2023, per Kintsugi; older guides still show 50,000). Foreign providers of electronic services to recipients in BiH must appoint a tax representative and register.

sources.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina - Corporate - Other taxes
sources.quote: Any person making taxable supplies of goods and services that exceeds or is likely to exceed a threshold of 100,000 konvertibilna marka (convertible mark or BAM) is required to register as a VAT payer.

D1_id_document.question: Identity documents residents use for KYC (gateways, banks, platforms)
D1_id_document.answer: National identity card: Lična Karta / Osobna iskaznica (Identity Card) (Wikipedia, compulsory-ID list). At the age of 16 in Bosnia and Herzegovina, one can obtain an ID card, but it does not grant any legal authority until turning 18 and then becomes mandatory and is to be carried at all times after turning 18. Banks and payment platforms usually also accept a passport; their exact lists were not captured.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
